tasks.short: Check supplier and agency invoices against orders and hours, code them in AFAS, release the Rabobank payment batch.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive by mail or PDF in the AFAS inbox; payment run on a fixed weekday.
steps: Open the scanned invoice in AFAS and check the supplier, IBAN and VAT
Match it to the purchase order or the agency's approved hours from the portal
Code the ledger account, cost centre and site
Chase approvers by Outlook for invoices without a match
Build and release the payment batch to Rabobank
drudgery: Typing invoice lines that the scan misread
Comparing agency invoice hours line by line to portal hours
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices with hundreds of flex worker lines that differ slightly from approved hours, and invoices without a PO.

lenses.faster: Reading, matching and coding disappear for matched invoices; the accountant spends about a third of today's time on exceptions and the batch release.
lenses.autonomous: A new invoice in the AFAS inbox starts extraction and a match against PO or portal hours; matched invoices within tolerance are queued, and the gate is the accountant releasing the Rabobank batch.
lenses.ambitious: A weekly agency-invoice check for each of the three sites against hours worked, so overbilling of flex workers is caught before payment instead of at year end; demand grows as it gets cheaper because peak season adds 150 extra workers.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping lines and comparing hour lists; the accountant wants more time on agency tariff disputes and supplier terms.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts; one match result with a clear reason per difference is enough.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from processing to owning match tolerances and the exception queue, with the right to set auto-approve thresholds per supplier together with the Controller; slightly more expert.
reach: Absorb the bookkeeper's AP exception handling for agency invoices; needs to learn the agency contracts and CAO tariff tables
Take over supplier master data checks (IBAN changes) from the bookkeepers; needs fraud-pattern knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a disputed agency charge or an IBAN change is legitimate, and holding a supplier to the contract.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a messy invoice into structured lines; the match against PO and portal hours and the tolerance rules are fixed code.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice lands in the AFAS purchase invoice inbox or an agency invoice file is downloaded.
steps: Extract header and lines from the PDF or UBL
Match against PO, goods receipt or agency portal hours with fixed tolerances
Propose ledger account, cost centre and VAT code
Route mismatches with a stated reason to the approver
Accountant reviews the exception list and releases the payment batch
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves exceptions and releases the Rabobank batch; IBAN changes need a second person.
data_needed: Approved hours per agency per week
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice history with match result and approver, plus an exception log in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit offers scanning and recognition of purchase invoices.
A PDF is not an e-invoice; Dutch B2B e-invoicing is planned from 1 July 2030, which would make structured input the norm.

risks: Payment fraud through a changed IBAN slipping through an automatic match
Agency hour disputes hidden inside tolerance bands
research_questions: What share of current invoices match a PO or portal hours without any change?
Can the three agency portals export approved hours in a machine-readable form?
How many IBAN change requests per year, and how are they verified today?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the monthly accounts and statements for accuracy and completeness before they go to the Controller.

today.trigger: Month end close calendar and year end.
steps: Export trial balance and subledgers from AFAS to Excel
Tie subledgers to the general ledger
Compare balances with last month and budget and investigate big moves
Check that close items on the checklist are done
Write notes for the Controller
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel tie-outs each month
Hunting for the entry behind a variance
today.time_sinks: Tracing variances across files and sites, and redoing tie-outs when a late entry lands.

lenses.faster: Tie-outs and first variance explanations are prepared before the accountant starts; what stays is judging the flagged items and signing off, about 60% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar starts automatic tie-outs and a draft variance file each night of close; the gate is the accountant accepting each explanation.
lenses.ambitious: A mid-month soft close per site, so the Finance Director sees Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo results two weeks earlier; demand would grow because site managers ask for it once it exists.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding tie-out sheets; the accountant wants more time on what the numbers mean for the business.
lenses.options: Drafting alternative explanations for a large variance helps decide which one to test first.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from building tie-outs to reviewing exceptions and deciding which variances need correction, with the right to stop a close item; more expert.
reach: Take part of the FP&A Analyst's monthly actuals commentary; needs to learn the forecast drivers

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance matters to the business and spotting an assumption that makes a workpaper impossible to rebuild.
tasks.pattern_why: Tie-outs are fixed code; one model call drafts variance explanations from the entries behind them, checked against the tie-out.

in_practice.trigger: Close day 1 per the close calendar.
steps: Pull trial balance and subledgers from AFAS
Run fixed tie-outs and threshold checks
Draft explanations for variances above threshold, citing entries
Accountant reviews, corrects and signs off
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant signs off each tie-out and explanation before the Controller sees it.
in_practice.logs_to: Close workpaper folder in SharePoint with sign-off per item.

evidence.claim: On four month-end scenarios a model beat twelve licensed CPAs, but the tasks left out communication and tacit context.
On 160 US GAAP tasks the best model meets 61.8% of criteria; multi-step reasoning errors dominate.
Accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster across 79 firms.

risks: Plausible but wrong variance explanations accepted under time pressure
Unnoticed assumptions making workpapers impossible to rebuild
research_questions: How many hours of the close go into tie-outs versus explaining variances?
How often would a drafted explanation have been wrong on the last six closes?
Will the external auditor accept workpapers with model-drafted explanations?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, intercompany, AP, AR and suspense accounts and clear the differences.

today.trigger: Monthly close, and daily for the bank.
steps: Import Rabobank statements into AFAS
Match open items that auto-match missed
Reconcile intercompany between sites and balance sheet accounts in Excel
Investigate and book differences
File the reconciliation for review
drudgery: Matching bank lines with unclear references by hand
today.time_sinks: Customer payments covering several invoices and suspense items that sit for months.

lenses.faster: Matching and roll-forward disappear; the accountant handles the remaining unmatched items and reviews, roughly 45% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Each CAMT.053 statement and each close day trigger matching and a reconciliation draft; the gate is the accountant approving proposed clearing entries.
lenses.ambitious: Daily balance sheet reconciliations instead of monthly, so differences are found while people still remember the transaction; demand grows because a cheaper daily check shortens the close.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking bank lines; the accountant wants more time fixing the cause of recurring differences.
lenses.options: Several candidate matches for a multi-invoice payment, ranked, help the accountant choose the right one.
lenses.altitude: From matching items to owning the matching rules and deciding write-offs within a limit; more expert.
reach: Take over cash application exceptions from the Credit and Collections Officer; needs to learn customer payment habits

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is an error, a timing item or something to escalate, and calling the other side to resolve it.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching rules on amount, date, reference and counterparty can be written down; a model only helps word explanations for leftovers.

in_practice.trigger: Daily CAMT.053 import and close day 2.
steps: Import statement and open items
Apply matching rules including one-to-many
Propose clearing entries for matches and list leftovers with age
Accountant reviews leftovers and approves write-offs
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves any clearing or write-off entry above a set amount.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation record per account in SharePoint, entries in AFAS with source.

evidence.claim: Cash checks from CAMT.053 fit deterministic software at high autonomy.

risks: Over-broad matching rules hiding real errors
research_questions: What auto-match rate does AFAS reach today on Rabobank lines?
Which balance sheet accounts cause most differences each month?
Is the auditor satisfied with rule-based reconciliations and an exception log?

tasks.short: Check our books and processes for weak controls, wrong postings and inefficient procedures.

today.trigger: Quarterly internal control check, auditor findings, or a problem found in the close.
steps: Pick a sample of transactions from AFAS
Check postings against procedures and authorisation rules
Check segregation of duties in AFAS roles
Write findings and agree fixes with owners
drudgery: Pulling samples and checking them one by one
Comparing user role lists by hand
today.time_sinks: Sampling only covers a small share, so issues surface late at the audit.

lenses.faster: Sampling disappears because tests run over every transaction; review of hits and writing findings stay, about 65% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly run tests all transactions for duplicates, split invoices, IBAN changes and segregation of duties; the gate is the accountant deciding which hits are findings.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous control tests that the external auditor can rely on, lowering audit fees and audit adjustments; demand grows as each test is cheap to add.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses pulling samples; the accountant wants more time talking with process owners about fixes.
lenses.options: Not much; the decision is about which hits are real.
lenses.altitude: From sampler to designer of the control test set, with the right to propose AFAS role changes to the Controller; more expert.
reach: Take part of the external auditor's interim testing prep; needs audit methodology
Check payroll postings for the Payroll Specialist; needs payroll and CAO knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Interviewing staff about how work is really done and judging whether a pattern is fraud, error or a sensible workaround.
tasks.pattern_why: Control tests such as duplicates and segregation of duties are written rules run over all data.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly after close, or ad hoc on request of the Controller.
steps: Extract all journals, invoices and user roles from AFAS
Run the fixed test set
Rank hits by amount and risk
Accountant reviews hits and writes findings
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller decide which hits become findings and actions.
data_needed: AFAS user roles and approvals log
in_practice.logs_to: Control test log and findings register in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Internal control tests over every transaction fit deterministic software at autonomy 4; interviews stay human.

risks: Too many false hits so real ones are ignored
Access to all transactions including payroll data needs AVG/GDPR controls
research_questions: Which audit findings of the last two years would full-population tests have caught?
Can AFAS export role and approval logs?
What false hit rate makes the review unworkable?

tasks.short: Book month-end accruals, deferrals and corrections, including flex worker hours not yet invoiced.

steps: List recurring accruals and deferrals in Excel
Estimate uninvoiced agency hours from portal data
Calculate corrections found in reconciliations
Enter journals in AFAS with support
Reverse prior month accruals
today.time_sinks: Estimating agency accruals across three agencies and three sites under time pressure.

lenses.faster: Drafts with support attached are ready on day 1; the accountant reviews and posts, about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Close day 1 triggers drafted entries from portal hours, contracts and reconciliations; nothing posts until the accountant approves.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly agency cost accruals per site so site managers see real flex labour cost during peak season; demand grows when cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rekeying recurring journals; the accountant wants more time on judgement entries.
lenses.options: Two or three accrual estimates on different assumptions help decide the booked amount for uncertain items.
lenses.altitude: From preparing entries to approving them and setting the accrual method, with posting rights over drafted entries; more expert.
reach: Take over the Payroll Specialist's holiday pay and CAO accrual entries; needs CAO knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Judging estimates, materiality and what the auditor will accept.
tasks.pattern_why: One call drafts entries with support from known sources; the tie-out gate checks them before posting.

steps: Collect portal hours, contracts and reconciliation differences
Draft entries with calculation and source
Check entries balance and tie to source
Accountant approves and posts in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves each entry; estimates above a threshold go to the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal with attached workpaper and approver.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and recommends revenue schedules while teams stay responsible for review.
Estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.

risks: More audit adjustments if review slips
research_questions: How many adjusting entries per month are recurring versus judgement?
How close were past agency accruals to final invoices?
Does AFAS support a draft-journal approval flow?

tasks.short: Guide the bookkeepers on filing, posting and sending financial records, and check their work.

today.trigger: Daily questions from bookkeepers and month-end deadlines.
steps: Answer posting and filing questions in Teams
Assign close tasks and check progress
Review samples of bookkeeper work
Explain procedure changes
drudgery: Answering the same procedure question again
today.time_sinks: Interruptions and status chasing in close week.

lenses.faster: Procedure questions get answered from the SharePoint manual and status is visible on a close checklist; coaching stays, about 80% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone; a checklist tracker flags late tasks and the accountant decides.
lenses.ambitious: A searchable procedure assistant for the three bookkeepers and site admin staff who post costs, served for the first time; demand grows with use.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses repeating answers and chasing status; the accountant wants more coaching time.
lenses.altitude: The accountant becomes the owner of the procedure manual and close plan with the right to assign close tasks; about as expert.
reach: Absorb part of the Controller's close planning; needs planning and people skills

tasks.human_edge: Coaching, setting priorities and noticing when someone is overloaded or unsure.
tasks.pattern_why: The person leads the team; AI only drafts answers and status overviews.

in_practice.trigger: A bookkeeper question in Teams or a close task past its date.
steps: Draft an answer from the procedure manual with the source
Accountant checks and sends
Close tracker flags overdue tasks
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant sends every answer and decides on task changes.
in_practice.logs_to: Close checklist in SharePoint and Teams thread.

evidence.claim: Recordkeeping and directing filing staff fits copilot at autonomy 2.

research_questions: How many hours a week go to repeat questions?
Is the procedure manual complete enough to answer from?

tasks.short: Maintain the chart of accounts and cost centres and assign entries to the right account.

today.trigger: New activities, sites or cost types, and misposted entries found at close.
steps: Receive requests for new accounts or cost centres
Decide structure and create them in AFAS
Recode misposted entries
Update the account mapping for Power BI
drudgery: Keeping the Power BI mapping in sync
today.time_sinks: Misposting found late and recoding across many lines.

lenses.faster: Suggested accounts at entry and a monthly scan for likely misposting remove most recoding; about half of today's time stays.
lenses.autonomous: Each new entry gets an account suggestion with confidence; low confidence goes to a person, account structure changes stay manual.
lenses.ambitious: Cost per site and per customer contract made reliable enough for pricing decisions by sales; demand grows when accurate.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses recoding; the accountant wants to design a better structure.
lenses.options: Several chart designs for a new site or service help choose the reporting structure.
lenses.altitude: Owner of the account structure and mapping with the right to approve new accounts; more expert.
reach: Take over the Power BI finance mapping from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst; needs basic Power BI modelling

tasks.human_edge: Designing a structure that serves reporting, tax and management at the same time.
tasks.pattern_why: A model call suggests the account from description and history; the structure itself is a human decision.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice line or journal without an account, or month-end misposting scan.
steps: Suggest account and cost centre from history
Auto-accept above a confidence level
Queue low confidence for review
Accountant approves changes to the chart
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves low-confidence suggestions and all chart changes.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS audit trail and change log in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Account assignment fits llm_step with a tie-out gate at autonomy 3.

risks: Repeating past misposting learned from history
VAT codes linked to wrong accounts
research_questions: How many recodings per month today?
How accurate would suggestions have been on last year's postings?

tasks.short: Improve and document how we record transactions in AFAS and our close process, including e-invoicing and SBR filing.

today.trigger: Process problems, new laws, AFAS updates or audit findings.
steps: Analyse the current process and its problems
Design changes to AFAS setup or workflows
Test and document in SharePoint
Train colleagues
today.time_sinks: Documentation that is never up to date and testing changes by hand.

lenses.faster: Drafted documentation, test scripts and small automations built with AI coding cut build time; design and testing decisions stay, about 70%.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous; the accountant leads every change.
lenses.ambitious: Prepare Noordhaven for B2B e-invoicing from 2030 and SBR filing, a new service to the Finance Director; demand grows with each new rule.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing documentation by hand; the accountant wants more time on process design.
lenses.options: Alternative process designs compared on effort and control risk help pick one.
lenses.altitude: Becomes the finance process designer who builds small tools with AI coding and decides AFAS setup changes with the Controller; more expert.
reach: Absorb simple AFAS configuration from IT; needs AFAS admin training
Build reports for FP&A; needs Power BI

tasks.human_edge: Knowing how people actually work and what the auditor and the law require.
tasks.pattern_why: The person designs; AI drafts documents, tests and small scripts.

in_practice.trigger: Change request, audit finding or new rule.
steps: Draft the process change and documentation
Generate test cases
Accountant tests and approves
Publish to SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller approve before go-live.

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing is planned from 1 July 2030, reporting from 2031.
Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025 and AFAS cannot file this for them.

risks: Documentation that looks complete but is wrong
research_questions: Which process changes are planned for the next two years?
Who builds and maintains small finance tools today?

role.altitude: From preparing and checking entries to designing the matching rules, tie-outs and control tests that check every entry, and judging the exceptions they raise.
reach: Bookkeeper AP exceptions for agency invoices
Credit and Collections cash application exceptions
role.ceiling_note: Limited by judgement on estimates, tax and audit acceptance, by multi-step reasoning errors in models, and by data quality from agency portals.
role.ambitious_version: A continuous close: daily reconciliations, weekly agency accruals per site and full-population control tests, so the month closes in a few days with a forecast the business trusts.
